title: Unraveling the Molecular Mechanisms of Benzo(a)pyrene (BaP)-Induced Ovarian-Related Disorders: Integrating Computational Predictions and Experimental Validation.
authors: Ma, Mengwei; Qi, Tao; Lin, Yuqiang; He, Haiyan; Lei, Haotian; Gao, Rufei; Han, Fei; Liu, Taihang; Xu, Hanting; Chen, Xuemei
one_liner_zh: 该研究整合网络毒理学、分子对接与MD模拟预测BaP与EGFR/ESR1/STAT3蛋白的结合，但对象为小分子-蛋白互作而非蛋白质-DNA互作，且无TF-DNA结合建模，仅方法部分可借鉴。
abstract: The ovaries are crucial reproductive organs that regulate the menstrual cycle and support pregnancy through the production of steroid hormones. They are highly susceptible to various environmental pollutants, which can lead to ovarian disorders. Luteal phase defect (LPD) and premature ovarian failure (POF) are common ovarian disorders in women. In this study, we integrate network toxicology with molecular docking and molecular dynamics simulations to elucidate the toxicological mechanisms of Benzo(a)pyrene (BaP), a widespread endocrine disruptor, in LPD and POF. Through systematic data mining of the GeneCards and OMIM databases, we identified 1336 targets associated with LPD and 2066 targets related to POF, as well as 220 BaP targets. Venn diagram analysis revealed 36 potential targets for BaP-induced LPD and 43 for BaP-induced POF. GO and KEGG enrichment analyses suggest that BaP-induced LPD and POF may share toxicological mechanisms. PPI network visualization indicated that EGFR, ESR1, and STAT3 are critical common targets for BaP-induced LPD and POF. Molecular docking and molecular dynamics simulations revealed that BaP exhibits strong binding affinity with all three core genes. In KGN cells modeling LPD and POF phenotypes, cellular experiments confirmed that BaP downregulated EGFR and ESR1 expression while upregulating STAT3 expression, thereby supporting the reliability of these targets in BaP-induced ovarian dysfunction. These findings provide insights into BaP-induced reproductive toxicity and offer a foundation for targeted clinical interventions to mitigate the effects of environmental pollutants on women's reproductive health.
abstract_zh: 卵巢是关键的生殖器官，通过产生类固醇激素调节月经周期并支持妊娠。它们极易受到各种环境污染物影响，从而导致卵巢疾病。黄体期缺陷（LPD）和卵巢早衰（POF）是女性中常见的卵巢疾病。在本研究中，我们整合网络毒理学与分子对接和分子动力学模拟，以阐明苯并(a)芘（BaP）——一种广泛存在的内分泌干扰物——在LPD和POF中的毒理学机制。通过对GeneCards和OMIM数据库的系统数据挖掘，我们鉴定了与LPD相关的1336个靶点、与POF相关的2066个靶点，以及220个BaP靶点。维恩图分析揭示了BaP诱导LPD的36个潜在靶点和BaP诱导POF的43个潜在靶点。GO和KEGG富集分析表明，BaP诱导的LPD和POF可能共享毒理学机制。PPI网络可视化显示，EGFR、ESR1和STAT3是BaP诱导LPD和POF的关键共同靶点。分子对接和分子动力学模拟揭示，BaP与所有三个核心基因表现出强结合亲和力。在模拟LPD和POF表型的KGN细胞中，细胞实验证实BaP下调EGFR和ESR1表达，同时上调STAT3表达，从而支持了这些靶点在BaP诱导卵巢功能障碍中的可靠性。这些发现为BaP诱导的生殖毒性提供了见解，并为靶向临床干预以减轻环境污染物对女性生殖健康的影响奠定了基础。
